explanation: Store distinct input values as signed 64-bit hash keys. Remove one seed, then erase each consecutive neighbor below and above it while counting the component. Wide neighbor arithmetic keeps signed 32-bit endpoints separate, so INT_MIN and INT_MAX never become artificial neighbors. Each distinct input is consumed once.
timeComplexity: O(n) expected time for n input entries.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C++ implementation, independently authored from the public EPI problem contract and the repository-authored C# algorithm. Uses unchanged local EPI Judge serialization and test framework APIs; upstream reference sources are not modified.
